record.paper_title: Option Pricing: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: asset selection for generalized safe-price hedging
record.original_question: Consider an option with payoff P_T at time T. A writer wants to form a static hedging portfolio V_t at time 0 by selecting k assets from n available assets, where k is not fixed in advance, buying nonnegative amounts a_i of the selected assets S_i, and placing a nonnegative amount b in a bank account. The portfolio is intended to minimize initial cost V_0 = sum_i a_i S_i(0) + b while satisfying one or more risk constraints such as E(P_T) <= E(V_T), P(P_T <= V_T) >= p for a chosen p in (0, 1), or Var(V_T) <= sigma for a chosen sigma > 0. How should the writer choose the subset of k assets and their weights to create the best possible portfolio, and can this choice be standardized as a mathematical methodology based on past market data?

such that E(PT) ≤ E(VT) or/and P(PT ≤ VT) ≥ p or/and Var(VT) ≤ σ or any combination of the above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space and fix a time horizon $T>0$. Consider an option with non-negative payoff $P_T$, a $\mathcal{F}_T$-measurable random variable. There are $n$ tradable assets whose price processes are $S_1(t),\dots,S_n(t)$, $t\in[0,T]$, with $S_i(0)>0$ known, together with a bank account paying no interest (or a fixed deterministic interest rate). A writer of the option wishes to construct, at time $0$, a static hedging portfolio of the form
$$V_t \;=\; \sum_{i\in I} a_i\, S_i(t) \;+\; b,$$
where $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ is a subset (of cardinality $k=|I|$ that is not fixed in advance), the weights $a_i\ge 0$ for $i\in I$, and $b\ge 0$ is the amount placed in the bank account. 

Given parameters $p\in(0,1)$ and $\sigma>0$, the goal is to solve
$$\min_{I,\,(a_i)_{i\in I},\,b} \; V_0 \;=\; \sum_{i\in I} a_i\, S_i(0) + b$$
subject to one or several of the risk constraints
$$\mathbb{E}[P_T]\;\le\;\mathbb{E}[V_T], \qquad \mathbb{P}(P_T\le V_T)\;\ge\;p, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(V_T)\;\le\;\sigma,$$
or any conjunction of these.

The problem is twofold:
(a) Determine, for given joint distribution of $(P_T,S_1(T),\dots,S_n(T))$, how the writer should select the subset $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ and the weights $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ and $b$ that achieve the minimum initial cost subject to the chosen risk constraints.
(b) Provide a standardized mathematical methodology that, using only past market data of the $n$ assets and the option, produces such an optimal subset and weights.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem in the source where it appears (a collection of open problems on option pricing). No published solution providing a general, standardized methodology under the combined expectation, probability, and variance constraints with subset selection has been located in the literature; related work on static superhedging and sparse portfolio selection addresses special cases but not the full formulation. Status appears to remain open.
